# Motivation

## Nature is invisible in the accounts

- Ecosystems supply services the economy depends on, from pollination and soil retention to coastal protection and carbon storage, yet none of them appear in standard national accounts.
- Unmeasured, the loss of these services surfaces only later — as lower yields, higher damages and higher prices.
- The Gross Ecosystem Product (GEP) account values what ecosystems supply, country by country and service by service, so natural capital can be tracked alongside GDP.
- The same service models also drive scenario analysis: how climate and land-use scenarios change the services economies depend on, feeding the macroeconomic pipelines.

## Why one reviewed library

- Different GEP service models were developed by different contributors in different repositories, with their own layout, path conventions and aggregation choices.
- The library brings them into one repository with one layout: every service runs the same way, reproduces its numbers on rerun, and writes the same per-country table the GEP account reads.
- A GEP account changes decisions only if every number can be traced to the model that produced it; the totals table carries each service's verification status.
- Central banks and finance ministries are asked to price nature risk, and the scenarios they use carry no ecosystem-service feedback; the pipeline this library feeds adds one.

# What global_invest is

## One module per service: GEP always, a shock where the science allows

- The library holds one folder per ecosystem service, all on the same file convention.
- Every one of the {{< meta n_services >}} services now carries its GEP method in the library, with its input data copied into the shared base data.
- Services whose science supports it also produce a scenario shock for the macroeconomic pipeline; not all can be made into shocks.
- A service with both outputs computes them from the same functions file — one implementation, so the valuation and the shock cannot disagree.
- The library is scenario agnostic: a caller injects its own scenario naming through scenario maps and configuration.

## The mental model: a service module reads like a paper

| File | In paper terms |
|---|---|
| functions.py | The equations — pure science; knows nothing about folders or projects. |
| tasks.py | The estimation steps — each caches its output and skips itself when already done. |
| initialize.py | The table of contents, plus the plug other pipelines graft in. |
| run_\<service\>.py | The main script — opens a workspace and goes. Thin on purpose. |
| method.qmd | The methods section — rendered from the code. |

- The three CSVs are the calibration tables. es_config states what each model reads and how it prices; es_scenarios states which scenarios and maps; es_parameters holds the run parameters and machine locations.
- One rule ties data to code: a CSV cell is a default, and whatever the caller already set prevails.

## The template every service follows

- One runner per task tree, and every run file shares one anatomy: build_task_tree names the pipeline, tasks publish their own inputs, and the runner stays thin.
- Configuration is data, in two shared CSVs.
- es_config.csv: one row per service, in the GEP formula's own vocabulary — quantity, price, attribution, land base, base year, price convention — plus the crosswalk to the status sheet.
- es_scenarios_test.csv: the standard SEALS scenarios, with matching test maps shipped, so a standalone shock run works on any machine.
- A pipeline such as ngfs_pnas drives the same tasks from its own scenarios file; the CSVs only fill what it leaves unset.
- A task begins by naming its own inputs — not machine paths, but references into the shared base data (the next slide). Because every task carries its own input list, it works wherever it is grafted; this holds for every service now.
- Results aggregate to one row per country (r250). Sub-national tables (r264, marine r566) serve as computation surfaces and maps — their rows are never summed into totals.

## How a run finds its data

- Every input is a reference path relative to the shared base data, and each machine resolves it for itself: the task's own directory first (so finished work is found and skipped), then the project's input folder, then the machine's base_data, then the cloud fallback.
- A run therefore carries no absolute paths. The same run file works on a laptop, on the cluster, or on any machine that stages the same base data — the recreation port and the landslide cluster run rely on this.
- Tasks cache their output in the project directory and skip themselves when it already exists, so a rerun recomputes nothing and an interrupted run resumes where it stopped.

## Two callers, one science

- Each service module serves two callers: the GEP account reads the valuation (one row per country), and the macroeconomic pipeline reads the scenario shock (a table of productivity deviations for GTAP).
- Both read the same functions file, so a change to the science reaches the account and the scenarios at once.
- Not every service's science supports a shock, but every service is expected to reach a GEP valuation.

## How a pipeline grafts a service

- A caller grafts a service with one call — add_\<service\>_tasks(p) after its land-use step — and the service's tasks slot into the caller's own task tree.
- The caller's configuration prevails over the shipped CSVs (the rule from the mental-model slide), so the library never needs to know its callers' naming.
- The standalone runners use the same graft, so a bug found and fixed in a service's own run is fixed in the pipeline too — nothing changes between the two.

## The configuration table itself (es_config.csv)

- One row per service; the columns are the GEP formula's roles — Q = quantity input, P = price input, λ = attribution input, land = the LULC base — plus the crosswalk to this group's status sheet. An empty cell means the role does not apply.

| service | sheet crosswalk | base year | price convention | Q | P | λ | land |

| terrestrial_carbon | global_climate_regulation / terrestrial | 2019 | rental scc r2% | carbon zones raster | prices xlsx | | esa 2019 |
| coastal_carbon | global_climate_regulation / coastal | 2019 | rental scc r2% | | prices xlsx | | |

# Where things stand

## The state in three numbers

- **{{< meta n_services >}} services are in the library.** Thirteen of them (plus the subsistence fisheries component) replicate a committed reference or the manuscript.
- **Four await one file to finish verification** — recreation, commercial fisheries, erosion, landslide each need a reference output or input we could not find.
- **Three carry an open source or definition question** (pollination, renewable energy, coastal protection), and **one is quarantined** (livestock, pending its method inputs).

## How every GEP number is built

- Every service's number is the same construction: a QUANTITY of service delivered, times a PRICE, times NATURE'S SHARE of it — summed to one row per country.
- Worked example, terrestrial carbon: the quantity is tons of carbon stored (a density table over the land-cover map); the price is the rental social cost of carbon; nature's share is one, because storage is entirely nature's work. Result: {{< meta terrestrial_total >}}.
- The three parts differ per service — recreation's quantity is visits and its price is travel cost; livestock's nature share is the ecosystem-provided part of feed — but the construction never changes, which is why one configuration table (quantity, price, attribution) can describe every service.
- Where a part is missing or contested, that is the service's open question — the slides ahead are organized around them.

## Verification discipline, and what it caught

- Every restructuring step had to reproduce a saved reference run before it counted as done. Before any merge, a check lists everything a branch would remove from the shared code, so nothing disappears silently.
- Automatic checks run continuously: every shock table is validated before it is written, every country aggregation is guarded against double-counting split countries, and every configuration row is covered by a test from the moment it is added.
- These checks found and fixed real errors: an aggregation double-count, a baseline spelled two ways, and a stale input in the erosion chain.
- Each service's number is verified against an anchor — the manuscript, the author's own output, or our saved reference run; the totals table names which.
- Fifteen of the {{< meta n_services >}} services carry their own test module (test_\<service\>.py), run on every change; the five accounting services and landslide are covered by the library-wide tests only — their service-level tests are a known gap. What each pins is listed in the appendix.

# The questions, service by service

## terrestrial_carbon: verified against the manuscript

- [What it does: sums the carbon stored by land ecosystems (a zone-by-class density table on the land-cover map) and prices it at the rental social cost of carbon. State: GEP replicates the manuscript to the dollar, {{< meta terrestrial_total >}} at 2019.]{.state}
- A double-count in the code overstated its total by 23.5 percent (split countries entered once per sub-region — China six times); the corrected aggregation reproduces the manuscript to the dollar.
- **No open questions.** This service is the template the others are held to.

## coastal_carbon: seaward pixels only, or the full habitat?

- [What it does: sums the carbon stored in mangroves, salt marshes and seagrass (mapped habitat times per-habitat density) and prices it like terrestrial carbon. State: replicates the author's design, mangrove component to the cent. One run, two totals: {{< meta coastal_eez >}} counting ocean-side rows only, {{< meta coastal_all >}} counting both sides.]{.state}
- **Q1 (design):** was EEZ-only chosen to avoid double-counting the landward pixels with terrestrial carbon? Most of the mapped habitat sits landward of the shoreline (97.5 percent of mangrove area, 84 percent of salt marsh), so including it multiplies the total by 4.5.
- **Q2 (inputs):** which exact seagrass and salt marsh input versions produced the report's {{< meta coastal_report >}}? Our replication gives {{< meta coastal_eez >}} with mangrove matching to the cent, and the report's own seagrass area (62.21 Mha) exceeds the published range it cites (16 to 26.7 Mha).
- **Q3: if both sides count, a landward mask must prevent double-counting with terrestrial carbon — does one exist?**

## Marine carbon: no module yet

- [State: the service sheet lists Terrestrial, Coastal, and Marine carbon. We found no marine module in any repository — correct us if one exists.]{.state}
- **Q1:** is marine carbon in scope for the account at all, and on what horizon?
- **Q2:** if yes, which data product drives it?
- **Q3:** most open-ocean carbon sits in the high seas, inside no country's EEZ. Which attribution convention should a per-country account use?
- The sheet lists one more subgroup under the same service, equally without a module we could find: **Other Non-Carbon GHG** — the same three questions apply.

## pollination: which definition is the GEP?

- [What it does: values the crop production attributable to wild pollinators — a sufficiency-weighted value raster built from pollinator habitat around cropland. State: built on the template and running; aggregation verified. Two defensible definitions, 28 times apart. NOT yet at the account's 2019 base year (the August 31 alignment): the value raster is 2023, and its regeneration at 2019 follows the definition decision.]{.state}
- **Q1:** is pollination's GEP the service nature currently delivers ({{< meta poll_raster >}}, the sufficiency-weighted raster) or the production value at stake ({{< meta poll_fao >}}, dependence-weighted FAO value)? The country ranking is identical; only the definition differs.
- **Q2:** the rasters on hand are 2023 and the account values at 2019. We would regenerate at 2019 once the definition is settled — and we can: the generation recipe is on hand.
- Erosion's GEP records the habitat-supplied share, so the raster-side definition is the internally consistent choice.

## erosion: interim inputs

- [What it does: values the soil that land cover keeps in place — prevented erosion mapped by the SDR model, valued through crop productivity. State: the full chain runs end to end and reconciles internally at {{< meta erosion_total >}}, PROVISIONAL. Sections A and B verified structurally; the valuation runs on interim inputs we built ourselves.]{.state}
- **Q1: needed — the exact FAO production-value and price series the submitted paper used.** Our chain runs on interim series we built ourselves; every number moves when the originals replace them.
- **Q2: needed — a per-country output table from the submission run.** With it we verify by exact replication, as extractive_materials was.
- Could it be at `/projects/standard/jajohns/shared/sediment_gep` on MSI — and can we get it? One copy settles both questions.

## erosion: one science, two products, three methods

- One biophysical chain feeds everything: InVEST's SDR model yields actual soil loss (USLE) and bare-soil loss (RKLS); their difference is the erosion the land cover prevents.
- Two products come from it. The GEP valuation runs the chain once on observed land cover (prevention shares, on-farm and upstream, valued per country). The scenario shock reruns it per scenario and year on the SEALS maps.
- The shock has two paths: static reads the frozen dependency table (the default today); dynamic recomputes the full chain per map — expensive, so each step saves its output and skips itself on rerun.
- Three shock methods are computed side by side and reported together: damage (thresholded area share), service (threshold-free, magnitude-weighted per crop), and service-threshold (service restricted to a fixed severe-pixel set) — the last is the default that becomes the GTAP shock, and one configuration row selects which.
- Two resolutions: a 6.45 km analysis grid that runs on a laptop, or native 300 m on a cluster — one configuration row switches them.
- The method's constants (the SES-11 thresholds) are named in code and await the author's confirmation; every number from this service is provisional until then.

The input stage is complete (all twelve global reprojections and the event panels); the compute-heavy remainder is running on the cluster.]{.state}

## fisheries: the RCP substitution

- [What it does: values commercial capture fisheries as the economic rent of the catch, and subsistence fisheries as the consumptive-use value of home catch. The shock file derives from DBEM (Cheung 2021), built from CWoN inputs. The GEP valuation is ported to Python from the source repo's 2026 CWoN-method script — FAO-based economic rent from the CWoN 2024 reproducibility package (FR_WLD_2024_195), deflated to 2019 USD, extrapolated to 2019 by each country's own 2009–2018 trend, floored at zero — PROVISIONAL until the source choice is confirmed.]{.state}
- **Q1: should the RCP8.5-for-RCP7.0 substitution stand, or is there a replacement?** The 8.5 series stands in because no 7.0 series exists.
- **Q2: which CWoN vintage produced the shock file (cwon_shocks.har)?** The valuation side is pinned by the port (CWoN 2024, FR_WLD_2024_195); the shock file's vintage is still unknown.
- **Q3: is the CWoN method the account's fisheries GEP?** It runs at {{< meta fisheries_total >}} for 2019 across 165 countries, on the two CWoN tables copied from the public World Bank package. Needed: the source pipeline's output CSV for replication; the FishStatJ pipeline is the alternative source.
- The subsistence component is also ported to Python: Lynch et al. (2024) consumptive-use value per country, {{< meta fisheries_subsistence_total >}} across 85 countries (Canada and China lead), replicating the source repository's committed output. Whether and how commercial and subsistence combine into the account's fisheries value is the open scope question.

## recreation: ported and running

- [State: ported from the source repository: seven tasks in the library template, method constants pinned by unit tests, aggregation directly on r250, data staged, first run complete. What it does: land-cover shares, protected areas and road access rank 1 km sites; a gravity model sends residents (daily) and allocated overnight stays (UNWTO — the UN World Tourism Organization's tourism statistics) into the high-quality sites; visits are valued at national fuel cost times travel distance.]{.state}
- **The remaining need: a reference per-country output.** We could not find the source pipeline's results_by_country.csv anywhere we can reach; one copy verifies the port by replication.
- **Q: did the travel-cost step intend kilometres?** It multiplies a USD-per-km fuel cost by a distance measured in the raster's pixel units (degrees), which understates values roughly a hundredfold; our first run totals $1.73bn where a corrected distance would give about a hundred times more. Ported faithfully; the reference output decides.

- **Q2: is the intended nature share the GLEAM-3 feed-share lambda (GLEAM — FAO's Global Livestock Environmental Assessment Model): ecosystem-provided feed over total feed, per country, as the repo's lambda.py computes?** If so, the answer is neither crop's coefficients nor pasture rents, and we implement it.
- **Q3: needed — the GLEAM feed-intake table (gleam3_dmi.xlsx) and one per-country output table.** The table records, for each country and animal type, how much feed livestock consume and from which sources — grass and roughage versus crops and concentrates; the lambda divides the ecosystem-provided part by the total. We could not find either in the repo; with both, the method lands in the library verified by replication.

## fire_protection: three variants

- [State: translated to Python from the GEP wildfire repo's R pipeline (function by function; the R source stays the reference). Per-country fire-persistence regressions (committed in the source repo) give three betas: baseline persistence, the nature-vs-human CAUSE difference, and the nature-vs-human AREA difference. Each beta times the country's 2018 burned area gives avoided acres in 2019, valued at EM-DAT wildfire damage per burned acre. The port reproduces the repo's committed per-country output to the float, 161 countries; the replication runs inside the test suite, so it re-verifies on every change.]{.state}
- **Q1: which of the three GEP variants is the account's fire_protection value?** Baseline persistence totals −$22.4bn and the cause difference −$1.3bn — both globally negative — while the area comparison totals +$16.7bn. The choice sets both the number and its sign; the cause difference is the module's provisional default, marked as such.
- **Q3: the regressions cover 161 of the account's 250 countries; the other 89 carry no value.** No data is not zero avoided damage — whether and how to treat them is an account question.

## air_filtration: one workbook, two services

- [State: new module. # Cross-cutting decisions

## Which services could gain scenario shocks

- Four services produce shocks today (the carbons, pollination, erosion, fisheries). For the rest, the question is whether a scenario lever exists and who holds the chain.
- Feasible now, days of work each: TIMBER (SEALS forest-area change times the value layers — light compute; one decision: sharing the forestry sector with the carbon shock without double-counting) and FIRE (its nature-vs-human-area coefficient is a land-use lever — light compute; one decision: mapping SEALS classes to its area definitions).
- Feasible now, compute-heavy: RECREATION (the chain runs on land-cover shares, so a shock is a rerun per SEALS scenario map — hours per scenario on a laptop, plus the receiving-sector decision). LANDSLIDE is the same idea at cluster scale (its stability model reads forest share), with mortality as a nonstandard economic channel.
- Not feasible for us: air filtration, sandstorm, urban cooling and flood control ride on upstream infrastructure (InMAP, city-level InVEST, the flood stack) — their chains were built to trace scenarios, but the capability sits with those pipelines. Water quality is the exception: an in-library NDR chain could be built the way erosion's SDR was — weeks, not days.
- Deliberately no shock, at any effort: crop and livestock (their scenario effects already arrive through the pollination and erosion channels — an own shock would double-count), the extractives (abiotic rents), the static accounting components.

## Four conventions the room can settle today

- **Maps:** country values on split-country polygons render partially (China shows one sixth). We propose dissolving to one polygon per country, a one-time cartographic artifact that can never double-count. Any objection?
- **Base year:** {{< meta n_services_at_2019 >}} of {{< meta n_services >}} services value at 2019; pollination's raster is 2023 and gets regenerated after its definition is settled. Confirm 2019 as the account's base year.
- **Subsistence:** crop, livestock, and fisheries carry subsistence subgroups in the service sheet. In scope or not, per service?
- **The universe crosswalk:** the sheet lists roughly 26 services; the library covers ten. We propose a tested crosswalk table (sheet label to module to output) instead of restructuring modules to mirror the sheet. And the sheet's label typos should be fixed before anything inherits them.

## The August 31 write-up pass maps onto today

- Colleen's housekeeping email (due August 31) asks every group for consistent parameters and clean write-ups. Today's answers complete most of it a week early.
- **2019 dollars:** confirms our base year; pollination's regeneration will follow the sheet's deflator-conversion guidance once its definition is settled.
- **CWON rental rates, not GTAP:** renewable and fisheries already use CWON. For extractive, this is context for the 0.49 question — if that factor is a rental-rate choice, the CWON guidance may answer it.
- **EPA VSL:** landslide values mortality, so one open item — which VSL does v0.2.0 use?
- **Zeros vs NAs:** our verification hit exactly this — extractive has 9 countries NA for missing WB data (documented), and coastal_protection currently fills unmatched countries with zero in a merge, which needs the true-zero-or-NA review the email asks for. We will do that pass on our modules.
- **Discount rate 2 percent with 1 and 3 sensitivity:** the carbon services' rental SCC embeds a discounting choice — worth confirming it matches.

## What happens with the answers

- Every answer starts an already-scoped step, most of them mechanical: reference outputs trigger exact-replication verification (erosion, landslide, livestock), decisions trigger one-pass conversions (crop's units, the map dissolve), and the definitional calls trigger the regenerations that are already written up (pollination at 2019, the shoreline diagnostic).
- The questions live in a tracked document, and each closes with a verified number or a recorded decision.
- Each answer extends the same reproducibility to one more service. The goal for the next session like this one: no questions slide at all.
